question: Do the historical Pagbilao gut-content thesis records provide accessible, species-specific natural-diet evidence that can be safely represented in Bangwit?

findings.leonardo1984: The official DLSU repository page identifies Veronica Julia J. Leonardo’s 1984 B.S. Biology thesis, Gut content of some Mangrove fishes from Pagbilao, Quezon (accession TU03117). It is a print-format record of 78 leaves held in the DLSU Learning Commons archive; the page says the document is not available online. The page contains no abstract, methods, fish names, sampling dates, or gut-content results.
findings.meijar1984: Pinto (1987) cites a separate 1984 DLSU thesis by S. M. Meijar titled Gut content analysis of five fish species from Pagbilao (Quezon) mangrove forest reserve, 51 pp. The exact DLSU repository entry was not located in this bounded search. Keep this citation separate from Leonardo’s thesis.
findings.dietInterpretation: These titles are promising primary-source leads for natural diet, but bibliographic metadata alone does not reveal prey items, fish taxa, methods, sample sizes, season, or uncertainty. A future gut-content result should remain sample- and place-specific; it is not a complete species-wide diet and must not be converted into a bait recommendation.
findings.reuse: No thesis full text or item-specific reuse permission was obtained. No diet labels, species assertions, tables, or derived claims are transcribed.

interpretation: Record both as historical diet-source leads only; the available evidence does not support a single food item for any fish species.
Do not merge the Leonardo and Meijar theses; their source-reported names and lengths differ.
Do not add diet filters to public species pages from these citations alone. Separate source-reported gut contents from general species ecology and from bait suggestions.
The Pagbilao mangrove locality is historical and broad; no station geometry, current fish presence, or present-day feeding behavior is inferred.
nextActions: If diet evidence is pursued, use the DLSU archive’s published access process to inspect each thesis separately; no request or contact was made in this review.
For any obtained thesis, extract fish identity, sample size, collection date/site, stomach-analysis method, prey categories, empty stomachs, and limitations before cross-checking taxonomy.
Keep any stomach-content result distinct from species-wide natural-diet summaries and separate from lure/bait suggestions.
Continue the national region-by-region inventory while marine, brackish, freshwater, wetland, diet, fishery-catch, and regulatory evidence remain separate.

sources.supports: Official DLSU title, author, year, degree, accession, physical format, shelf location, and notice that the thesis is not available online.
Pinto 1987 reference-list citation for a separate Meijar 1984 five-fish gut-content thesis; not the thesis text.
Primary published reference list that cites Leonardo and Meijar; it does not provide their gut-content findings.
